title: Clustering methods in manifoldsR (with emphasis on EVoC)
text: manifoldsR provides two clustering approaches (now): k-means (full Lloyd’s mini-batch) importantly EVoC (Embedding Vector Oriented Clustering). implemented Rust SIMD acceleration, heavy parallelism cache-friendly memory layouts speed. package also ships cluster evaluation metrics (ARI, silhouette score inertia) can assess results without load another package (course also made fast Rust… know drill now). K-means partitions data exactly k clusters iteratively assigning points nearest centroid recomputing centroids cluster means. full (Lloyd’s) implementation manifoldsR heavily optimised (original ann-search-rs). high-dimensional data (dim >= 96), defaults Hamerly’s algorithm: per-point upper lower distance bounds prune vast majority distance computations first iterations, GEMM-based assignment (defaulted dimensionality high enough) keeps remaining work cache-friendly. Euclidean distance, typically prunes 90%+ point-centroid comparisons 3-4 iterations, meaning convergence cost closer handful full passes theoretical worst case. cosine distance (Hamerly’s bounds apply, since cosine lacks triangle inequality), full GEMM reassignment performed iteration. Lower-dimensional data (dim < 96) falls back direct SIMD-accelerated loops, avoid GEMM kernel overhead small dimensions. (wish can actually control exact dispatch. params_kmeans() give tight control needed.) mini-batch variant (Sculley 2010) samples random subset points per iteration applies incremental centroid update decaying learning rate (eta = 1/count). appeal iteration cheap: batch_size distance computations instead n. practice, however, full version’s bound-based pruning aggressive mini-batch offer speed advantage data sets become large (roughly 10M+ points) cluster structure messy enough Hamerly’s pruning eliminate candidates. moderate scales (~1M), full version often converges faster wall-clock time. mini-batch differ meaningfully behaviour -specification k. incremental learning rate causes centroids near dense clusters stabilise quickly (counts grow large, shrinking eta), extra centroids low-density regions receive updates effectively starve. result mini-batch k-means robust setting k higher true number clusters, .e., naturally concentrates mass real structure rather forcing every centroid carve territory. EVoC (Embedding Vector Oriented Clustering) takes fundamentally different approach. constructs k-nearest neighbour graph, learns lower-dimensional embedding optimised clustering (similar UMAP, target dimensions different loss focus), applies hierarchical density-based clustering (spirit HDBSCAN) multi-layer persistence analysis. key advantage EVoC require specify number clusters – discovers automatically returns multiple layers granularity ranked persistence. also handles noise outliers naturally, assigning label -1. generate synthetic data set well-separated clusters 128 dimensions. lets us evaluate clustering quality known ground truth. visualisation throughout vignette, compute 2D UMAP embedding reuse colour different cluster assignments. Full k-means distributes points across 25 centroids, splitting true clusters two. Mini-batch k-means, due incremental learning rate, effectively lets centroids starve; settle low-density regions attract points. result closely mirrors true structure. Inertia (within-cluster sum squares) decreases monotonically k increases. “elbow”, point adding clusters stops yielding meaningful improvement, suggests reasonable k.   ARI peaks true number clusters degrades k-means forced split well-separated groups. EVoC require specifying k. discovers cluster structure automatically returns multiple layers granularity.  can appreciate EVoC identified (nearly) perfectly ground truth… also apparent ARI score ≥0.99. EVoC returns hierarchy clusterings different granularities, ranked persistence. Layers higher persistence scores represent stable cluster structures.  rough idea many clusters expect, can guide EVoC approx_n_clusters. performs binary search minimum cluster size parameter target approximately many clusters, returning single layer. Let’s just compare end methods  K-means requires specifying k produces exactly many clusters notion noise. EVoC discovers number clusters automatically, handles noise outliers, provides multiple granularity layers. well-separated clusters know k, methods perform well (mini batch k-means can superior pending underlying data structure). EVoC shines number clusters unknown data contains noise, .e., situations k-means requires manual tuning repeated runs different k values. mini-batch variant k-means offers practical middle ground large data sets: converges faster degrades gracefully k -specified, cost slightly less precise centroid placement.

title: Using diffusion maps
text: large datasets N x N diffusion operator eigendecomposition become prohibitive. landmark approach PHATE applies: select representative subset, eigendecompose L x L landmark operator, Nystroem-extend result back full dataset. Default 2048L landmarks, rationale PHATE (SIMD-friendly 2^x number downstream k-means landmark selection). landmark_method accepts three options PHATE: "spectral" (default): spectral-clustering-based selection, geometrically representative, expensive. "random": uniform random sampling, fast, uneven coverage non-uniform density. "density": dampened degree-weighted sampling, cheaper spectral, may miss rare branches.  cheaper random-landmark version:  trajectory topology recovered cases, minor differences uniformly branches sampled.

text: function generates kNN graph based given numeric matrix. Seven different algorithms implemented different speed accuracy trade-offs: "hnsw" - Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds vector search slower index generation (ammortises larger data sets) high precision. "annoy" - Approximate Nearest Neighbours Oh Yeah algorithm, faster index querying large data sets can slow. "nndescent" - Rust-based implementation PyNNDescent algorithm, good -rounder performs well large data sets. "balltree" - Ball tree structure exact search configurable budget. "ivf" - Inverted file index leverages k-means clustering probing clusters. "exhaustive" - Exact nearest neighbour search. "kmknn" - Fast exact nearest neighbour search using triangle inequality
